summary: Masao Shizutani was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He held posts as assistant professor (助教授) at Josai University and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1974).

Masaru Akimoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held posts at Kyoto Women's University, including as professor in the Faculty of Contemporary Society (attested 2002 and 2015).

Masashi Nagai studied Buddhist studies at Komazawa University (~1965–1969, PhD 1998). He served at Komazawa University as lecturer (1984), assistant professor (1988, 1994), professor emeritus (2017), and president (2019), and directed the Museum of Zen Culture and History (~2007–2011).

Masataka Suzuki studied at Keio University (~1968–1978) and held a post there (~1984–2015). A specialist in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology, he has served as lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Masataro Sawayanagi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1885–1888). He held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1897–1898), Tohoku University (~1911–1913), Kyushu University (~1911–1912), and Taisho University (~1926–1927).

Masato Kobayashi studied linguistics and Indology at Kyoto University (~1989–1995) and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona (~1995–2000). He was a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2000–2003).

Masatoshi Konishi studied at International Christian University (~1957–1961), University of Calcutta (~1961–1965), University of Tokyo (~1965–1970), and Rikkyo University (PhD 2009). A scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, he taught at Hosei University (1971–1984) and Rikkyo University (1984–2003).

Masatoshi Nagatomi worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, Kyoto University (~1947–1950), and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1951–1957, PhD), where he became Instructor of Sanskrit in 1958.

Masayuki Taira studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1979). Specializing in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology, he held posts at Kansai University (~1981–1995), Osaka University (~1995–2016), and Kyoto Tachibana University (~2016).

Masayuki Tsukimoto is a scholar of Japanology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2026.

Massimo Pallottino studied history and archaeology at Sapienza University of Rome (~1927–1931). He held academic posts at the University of Cagliari (~1945–1947) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1947–1980).

Masumi Mochizuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts at Minobusan University as a lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhism (attested 2001), professor (attested 2015), and specially appointed professor (attested 2026).

Mathieu Boisvert works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology, having studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth. He founded Université du Québec à Montréal and became a professor there in 1992.

Mathurin Veyssière de La Croze worked in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Indology. He served as librarian and antiquary at the Royal Library of Berlin (~1697–1739) and as librarian at Humboldt University of Berlin (1697).
Matteo Bartoli studied linguistics at the University of Vienna (~1895–1898) and under Heinrich Hübschmann (~1898–1900). He held a post at the University of Turin (~1907–1946).

Matthew B. Orsborn completed his PhD at the University of Hong Kong (2012) under Guang Xing and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa, also studying under Hsing Yun and Huishang. Attested in 2026, he is Professor and Head of International Affairs at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Matthew Clark completed his PhD at SOAS University of London (1999–2004) in Indology and religious studies, where he studied under Daud Ali and George Botterill.

Matthew Immergut studied under Culadasa (attested 2011) and works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He is attested in 2011 as Associate Professor of Sociology at Purchase College, State University of New York.

Matthew R. Sayers earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle (attested 2008) in Indology and religious studies. He held a post at Lebanon Valley College (attested 2013).

Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Osaka City University, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies, and Duke University (PhD attested 2015) under Richard M. Jaffe, Helen Baroni, Michel Mohr, and Amy L. Allocco.
